skill.name: skill-auditor
skill.description: Audits AI skill definitions for structure, metadata quality, completeness, resource organization, and potential decomposition into focused skills.
skill.summary: Validate skill structure, metadata, content quality, and decomposition needs with a bundled Python auditor.
skill.author: BarisSozen

security_audit.summary: All static detections are false positives caused by Markdown backticks or a validation error string. The bundled Python script performs local, read-only checks without subprocesses, network access, or file modifications. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

For automated fixes, use the audit script with `--fix` flag:
See `references/audit-criteria.md` for detailed scoring rubrics and decomposition guidelines.

content.user_title: Audit AI Skills for Quality and Structure
content.value_statement: Inconsistent skill structure makes reviews and packaging harder. This auditor checks metadata, content, resources, and decomposition signals with repeatable rules.
actual_capabilities: Discovers immediate child directories that contain a SKILL.md file.
Validates frontmatter presence, required name and description fields, and description length.
Checks required sections, word count, TODO placeholders, empty resource directories, and Python script permissions.
Scores each skill from zero to ten and identifies decomposition signals.
Audits one skill or a directory and produces readable or JSON-formatted reports.
limitations: Bulk discovery checks only immediate child directories.
Frontmatter checks use text matching instead of a YAML parser, which can misclassify complex metadata.
The documented --fix option is not implemented by the bundled script.
Rules assess structure and heuristics, not security, factual accuracy, or runtime behavior.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Skill
use_cases.description: Check a new skill for required metadata, sections, placeholders, and resource issues before packaging.

use_cases.title: Review a Skill Library
use_cases.description: Run consistent structural checks across immediate child skill directories and compare scores.

use_cases.title: Plan Skill Decomposition
use_cases.description: Use word count, workflow complexity, section count, and reference volume to identify possible splits.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the skill at [skill path] as a single skill. Summarize errors, warnings, score, and the three most important improvements.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants a focused review before sharing one skill.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Skill Directory
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit every immediate child skill in [directory]. Rank results by score, then summarize repeated metadata, structure, placeholder, and resource issues.
prompt_templates.scenario: A maintainer needs a consistent review across a skill library.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Decomposition
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [skill path] for decomposition. Assess word count, distinct concerns, workflow length, audiences, formats, and reusable components. Propose focused sub-skills only when justified.
prompt_templates.scenario: A technical lead is deciding whether a large skill needs separation.

prompt_templates.title: Combine Automated and Manual Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the structural audit on [directory], then apply the reference rubric manually. Separate deterministic failures from judgment calls and provide prioritized remediation for each skill.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced reviewer needs a release-readiness assessment with clear evidence.

output_examples.input: Audit the release-notes skill as a single skill.
Review all skills and identify decomposition candidates.
output: Six skills audited; average score: 8.2 out of 10.
One skill needs decomposition review because its workflow has nine steps.
Two skills need shorter or more specific descriptions.

best_practices: Run single-skill mode when the target directory itself contains SKILL.md.
Review warnings manually because the script uses simple text and regular-expression checks.
Treat decomposition output as a prompt for design review, not an automatic requirement.
anti_patterns: Do not expect the advertised --fix flag to modify files; the script does not implement it.
Do not treat a high quality score as proof of security or correctness.
Do not use bulk mode for deeply nested skills without checking discovery coverage.

faq.question: Does this skill modify files?
faq.answer: No. The bundled script reads SKILL.md files and prints reports; the documented --fix option is not implemented.

faq.question: What does the auditor check?
faq.answer: It checks metadata, required sections, word count, placeholders, resource directories, script permissions, and decomposition signals.

faq.question: Can it audit one skill?
faq.answer: Yes. Use single-skill mode and provide the directory containing that skill's SKILL.md file.

faq.question: Can it produce machine-readable output?
faq.answer: Yes. The JSON output mode reports individual results, validation flags, decomposition reasons, and summary scores.

faq.question: How is the quality score calculated?
faq.answer: Each skill starts at ten points. Fixed deductions apply for missing metadata, weak structure, placeholders, excessive length, and resource issues.

faq.question: Does a passing score confirm security?
faq.answer: No. The rules evaluate structural quality and simple heuristics, not vulnerabilities, malicious intent, or runtime safety.
